Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that there is an analytic extension L/K such that, for the scalar-extension map π : XL → X
and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,
      then f is CLD-psh.
Then h is classically pluriharmonic and locally R-PL. If X is pure-dimensional, then h is also
GJR harmonic.
Corollary 5.2. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that h is not classically pluriharmonic. For every analytic extension L/K, at least one of the
following failures occurs:

                                                 42

 (1) d0 d00 [hL ] 6= 0;

 (2) one of hL and −hL has nonnegative Hessian current but does not belong to the CLD-psh
     hierarchy.

For L = K, the ﬁrst alternative is impossible. Hence every negative answer to P06.2 furnishes,
in one of the two signs of h, a continuous zero-current function outside the CLD-psh hierarchy.
If X is pure-dimensional, this is a counterexample to the converse of Book Proposition 15.9.8
in its stated scope.

    This reduction neither pulls a continuous current through an arbitrary scalar extension
nor proves positive-current regularization. It identiﬁes those operations as distinct proof
obligations and shows that a negative answer to P06.2 produces a zero-current function outside
the CLD-psh hierarchy at the ground ﬁeld. In the pure-dimensional scope this would disprove
the missing nonsmooth converse in Book Proposition 15.9.8.

GJR harmonic. This does not supply locally twisted annular coordinates at the top or insert
annular stages at arbitrary intermediate levels of the tower.
     Annular geometry may also occur at the bottom. The general transfer statement Book
Proposition M.1.34 isolates the common exact descent, classical-pluriharmonic transfer, R-
harmonic transfer, and ﬁrst-current-rigidity transfer of the four allowed bundle types over an
arbitrary admissible base. Applying it to a globally coordinated curve-polyannulus product
gives Book Corollary M.1.53: after any such mixed tower, the top function still has the
unique logarithmic coeﬃcient formula over the original curve. Applying it instead to a locally
trivial curve-polyannulus bundle or a locally trivial mixed curve-polycylinder bundle gives
Book Corollary M.1.54, Book Corollary M.1.55, with classical pluriharmonicity, local R-PL
regularity, and GJR harmonicity but no global coeﬃcient formula. Thus locally twisted
annular coordinates are now allowed at the bottom of the mixed exact tower. The result
still requires their displayed analytic local trivializations and does not allow an annular stage
to be interleaved at an arbitrary later level, an annular ﬁbration without such charts, or an
arbitrary nonproduct germ.
     For globally coordinated annular products, the two endpoint orders can be fully interleaved.
In Book Theorem M.1.20, each stage of a ﬁnite boundaryless tower over the curve may be
either one of the four exact bundle types or a globally coordinated ﬁnite standard strict
open-polyannulus product. An induction preserves classical pluriharmonicity, R-harmonicity,
and ﬁrst-current rigidity at every level. It gives a unique normal form on the tower top
with one logarithmic term for every annular coordinate introduced anywhere in the tower;
the zero-current base coeﬃcient and all locally constant slope coeﬃcients live on the original
curve. Thus globally coordinated annular stages may now occur at arbitrary levels. For a
global normal form, the remaining obstruction is the transition monodromy of locally twisted
annulus bundles: the theorem does not choose global annular coordinates. For one locally
trivial polyannulus bundle over the curve, however, Book Proposition M.1.26 now identiﬁes the
coeﬃcient system on overlaps. The logarithmic coordinates transform by a locally constant
unimodular integer matrix and a vector of zero-current base functions. These data satisfy
the aﬃne cocycle law, deﬁne a rank-s local system of lattices, and make the local slope
vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for
every zero-current function. The gauges are not asserted to be logarithms of analytic units,
so this criterion does not manufacture global annular coordinates. Even when the full class
does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar
contraction with the radiance class vanishes. Its exact sequence also shows that an injective
contraction, and in particular the absence of parallel dual sections, forces unique descent of
every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen
aﬃne gauge splits this sequence.

     For the three regularity conclusions, part of that monodromy obstruction can be removed.
In Book Corollary M.1.33, one analytic open cover of the original curve is allowed to coordinate
every annular stage after base change. On each member of the cover, the whole restricted
tower is an instance of the interleaved theorem; the local conclusions therefore glue even
though the annular coordinates, radii, and product trivializations need not agree on overlaps.
Thus curve-controlled locally twisted annular stages may occur at arbitrary levels. The result
deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations
available only over arbitrary opens of intermediate tower levels, because such opens need not
retain the preceding tower or its paracompactness hypotheses.
     There is also a nonproduct endpoint-base range. If the base is a positive- dimensional
standard strict endpoint polycylinder and the ﬁbre is a locally trivial standard strict open
polydisc, then Book Proposition M.1.37 pulls every full zero-current function back from the
explicit aﬃne combination of the base annular logarithms. Thus it is classically pluriharmonic,
locally R-PL, and GJR harmonic. This allows open, closed, and half-closed annuli in the base,
but still does not treat an annular ﬁbre, a ﬁbration without the displayed local product charts,
or an equation only on a strict radial core. The same formula persists through every ﬁnite
tower of the displayed locally trivial strict open-polydisc bundles: Book Corollary M.1.56
ﬁrst descends the function to the endpoint-polycylinder base and then applies the endpoint
classiﬁcation. Each level must carry the stated local product charts; the nontrivial tower
result retains the formula together with local R-PL and GJR harmonicity, by propagating its
local curve-product charts. This still does not cover annular ﬁbres or ﬁbrations without them.

rated, strict, pure positive-dimensional open inverse image in the extended tropicalization of
a split toric variety, and let a locally trivial standard strict open-polydisc bundle carry a lift
of its maximal compact torus action. If the continuous zero-current function is invariant for
that lifted action, then Book Corollary M.1.63 ﬁrst descends it to an invariant zero-current
function on the toric base and then applies the split-toric boundary theorem. It is therefore
locally real-PL, Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ harmonic, and classically pluriharmonic. The action,
invariance, and actual local open-polydisc trivializations are hypotheses: this supplies no con-
clusion for noninvariant functions, nonsplit forms, annular ﬁbres, or arbitrary disc ﬁbrations.
The same conclusion persists through every ﬁnite tower of such bundles when the maximal
compact torus acts on every level and all bundle maps are equivariant: successive exact
descents preserve invariance and reduce to the same split-toric base theorem; see Book Corol-
lary M.1.64. The same bundle scope descends through a chosen complete extension that is the

it requires the full compatible tower, action, invariance, and current equation after that chosen
extension. It does not manufacture the extension or bundle chart, and supplies no automatic
ascent of a downstairs current equality. Its analytic-local form Book Corollary M.1.70 requires
that displayed structure only near each point of the total space; it makes no assertion when
such neighbourhood data are absent. The same localisation is valid for ﬁnite towers: Book

that every continuous current-psh function on every smooth proper algebraic curve over an

Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that there is an analytic extension L/K such that, for the scalar-extension map π : XL → X
and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,
      then f is CLD-psh.

notes.text:
The mathematical claim is the following curve-scope theorem. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued field, X any good separated strict boundaryless K-analytic space pure of dimension one, U any ordinary open in X, and h:U→R continuous and finite. If the actual ordinary CLD current D[h]=d'd''[h] vanishes, then h is GR-harmonic and classically pluriharmonic, G-locally real PL, and GJR harmonic. No perfectness, reducedness, normality, global properness, algebraicity, or input scalar-stability hypothesis is imposed. Classical pluriharmonicity has the full quantifiers: after every complete analytic extension L/K and every analytic curve map Y→U_L, both pulled-back signs are GR-subharmonic.

The authoritative complete draft is P06.2-argument.md in the assigned workspace. Its standalone typesetting is P06.2-partial.tex and its twice-compiled PDF is P06.2-partial.pdf. status.json has exactly id, status, exact_result, proof_file, concrete_gaps and records status=partial. self-audit.md, research-notes.md, source-manifest.json, and evidence/ contain the dependency audit, failed routes, hashes, environment, commands, and outputs. Rerun from the workspace with python3 prepare.py followed by python3 build-and-check.py. The workspace is /workspace/research/campaigns/round-13/P06.2-arbitrary-field-curve-recognition-continuation/artifacts/codex-mNUPp2.

The first proof obligation is ordinary-current transport. On a pure curve, vanishing means ∫hDψ=0 for every compact ordinary smooth scalar test ψ; the unknown Hessian is not presumed to be a measure. For a finite Galois scalar extension, average a test over the finite group using real coefficients. Full-fibre shrinking gives unit-moment descriptions near every downstairs point. Approximate their Euclidean coefficients through order two by polynomials. Scalar polarization expresses every averaged mixed polynomial as a finite combination of traces of powers of logarithms of product units. The orbit polynomial has downstairs coefficients. Its Newton hull expresses these traces as piecewise polynomial functions of the nonzero coefficient valuations; coefficients vanishing at the selected point are omitted only after a strict inequality proves they cannot enter the lower hull.

Those Newton-hull functions are C1: when collinear segments merge, their gradients telescope. Their locally bounded chamber Hessians have no singular face contribution. Mollification converges in the tangent Hessian on every calibrated curve segment, including segments wholly contained in collision walls. On an enlarged moment chart, the positive top form Σd't_i∧d''t_i dominates the differentiated error on the actual supporting skeleton. Bounded convergence yields carrier total-variation convergence before any signed pushforward. Inner cutoffs may depend on polynomial degree, but every approximate support stays inside one fixed outer compact set. Thus pairing the error with any continuous finite h tends to zero. CLD14.3.6 and 15.3.1 transport pulled-back smooth top measures with no scalar degree factor. The separate same-carrier field-restriction calibration has the full finite degree; it is used only to justify the group action on the upstairs pairing. This proves finite separable ascent, with normal-closure descent handling non-Galois stages.

For a finite purely inseparable extension F/K, choose q=p^e with F^q⊂K. In the actual algebra A⊗K F every element has its qth power in A. Scalar projection is a homeomorphism, and each upstairs unit logarithm is q^-1 times a downstairs unit logarithm. Consequently compact scalar tests descend exactly. Every finite algebraic extension is treated through its actual embedded separable/purely inseparable tower, including all nilpotents.

For L equal to the completion of an algebraic extension M/K, completed-tensor density approximates finitely many analytic functions by functions over a finite embedded stage. A positive lower bound for the weighted maximum of a rational system's denominator and numerators makes sufficiently small perturbations preserve both the full weak conjunction and its strict locus exactly. On a compact rational domain, approximation below each unit's positive minimum preserves its norm exactly. The same smooth coefficient therefore defines a finite-stage scalar section whose pullback is the original section. A common finite stage and an explicit finite compact partition produce exact global descent of every compact ordinary scalar test. Compact inverse images and local purity are checked separately. The calibrated smooth top-measure identity then proves completed-algebraic ascent and descent of the actual current equation.

The second obligation is recognition, separate from transport. Equip an algebraic closure of K with its extending valuation and complete it to C. The draft proves C algebraically closed: approximate any monic polynomial by monic polynomials over the algebraic closure with rapidly decreasing coefficient errors; recursively choose roots whose successive distances tend to zero using the factored evaluation bound. Their bounded Cauchy sequence converges to a root. C is complete and nontrivially valued because it contains K isometrically. The transport theorem therefore gives D[h_C]=0 on the actual pure curve U_C.

For algebraically closed recognition, CLD16.6.3 decomposes integration into reduced components with their original generic Artinian lengths. Closed-embedding compact tests lift by analytic-unit lifting and compact cutoffs. Away from the finite rigid intersections, the current equation separates each component with its actual positive weight. Rigid scalar test germs are locally constant: the minimal polynomial of a unit's value forces its norm to remain constant on a sufficiently small neighbourhood. At a rigid point a, a regular analytic function with singleton zero fibre gives shrinking smooth cutoffs χ_m with uniformly bounded variation of Dχ_m and zero integral. CLD14.7.2 applies with target dimension one and an already S1 source; the bound contains the actual length times the full residue-field degree. A current supported at a is therefore cψ(a) on scalar tests, and continuity gives |c|≤M sup_supportχ_m|h-h(a)|→0. This removes rigid punctures without assuming D[h] is a measure.

Normalization is an actual isomorphism outside a locally finite rigid set: a common regular denominator clears its finite integral-closure generators. Transport on that isomorphism locus followed by puncture removal proves the upstairs equation. Over the algebraically closed field the normalization is smooth. Van der Put's Theorem1.1 applies only to a connected normal one-dimensional strict affinoid over that algebraically closed complete field. Thuillier's explicit Berkovich-domain formulation and the separated boundaryless interior equality identify actual ordinary neighbourhoods with ordinary opens of smooth proper algebraic curves. Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, Theorem4.7 applies exactly there: a continuous current-psh function is Thuillier-subharmonic. Her algebraic moment tests are ordinary analytic CLD tests with the same canonical integration. The zero equation supplies positivity for both signs. Dirichlet comparison recognizes harmonicity. GR3.14(7) descends already recognized harmonicity through normalization and the reduction immersion.

Full field quantifiers are checked after recognition. For any analytic extension L/K, embed the algebraic closure of K into an algebraic closure of L and complete the latter to a common complete field F containing C and L isometrically. F/C is not asserted algebraic. GR3.5(7), whose full proof is included, descends subharmonicity using this joint field and compact harmonic-majorant comparison on smooth strict probes. GR3.14(6), 4.1.2, 4.2(5), and 7.2(6) then give the full recognized-function descent. GR3.15 applies over the original nontrivially valued K to every strict analytic curve and yields real PL plus numerical triviality of all residual classes, precisely GJR harmonicity. The historical GJR references in GR3.15 are explicitly matched to the cached Lemma5.4(3) and Corollary5.12 statements and proof bodies. No weak-current substitution or ordinary smooth harmonic approximation is made.

notes.detailedSummary: Using n1's arbitrary-field intrinsic recognition, the draft proves harmonicity of h∘f for every analytic K-map from a separated smooth strict curve into an ordinary open of a pure ambient space in the original P06.2 scope. It reconstructs intrinsic restriction to closed analytic curves through positive effective cuts with actual component lengths, continuous multiplication of positive weak limits, an S1 Poincare–Lelong proof, compact test lifting, and rigid puncture removal. The local-image proof gives either a rigid constant map or an actual finite map onto a reduced closed pure curve image, with analytic surjectivity and a finite normalization lift checked. Applying recognition directly to the image avoids assuming its normalization smooth over imperfect K. The resulting probe function is Thuillier/GR harmonic, classically pluriharmonic, G-locally real PL, and GJR harmonic. Probes into scalar-extended higher-dimensional spaces remain outside this conclusion.
notes.text:
Assuming the curve theorem proved in n1, the additional mathematical claim is this: over every complete nontrivially valued K, let X be good separated strict boundaryless and pure of dimension n≥1, U⊂X ordinary open, and h:U→R continuous finite with actual ordinary CLD D[h]=0. For every analytic K-map f:Y→U from a separated smooth strict K-analytic curve, h∘f is Thuillier harmonic and GR-harmonic, classically pluriharmonic on Y, G-locally real PL, and GJR harmonic. Smooth includes absence of absolute analytic boundary. This is Theorem P in P06.2-argument.md; it uses n1's result and no previous solver-note theorem.

The restriction argument is intrinsic. On the ordinary interior of a strict affinoid neighbourhood, decompose the ambient integration cycle into reduced pure components with their actual generic lengths. Reduced noetherian rings satisfy S1 by finite prime avoidance. The draft proves Poincare–Lelong on such S1 sources from CLD14.7.2 with target dimension one and Green's formula. Its compact calibrated product near f=0 retains the actual zero-fibre lengths; the inner face gives the divisor integral and side faces vanish by dimension. The unsupported assertion in CLD16.7.5 that one regular element forces an arbitrary ring to be S1 is excluded.

For a regular cutting function on every component of a positive r-dimensional integration cycle S, use smooth convex truncations w_m of log|f| and the positive doubly closed form α_m=Dw_m. The currents α_m∧S converge to the effective component divisor cycle S_f. Continuous multiplication preserves this positive weak convergence: for a fixed compact symmetric test, a positive smooth coefficient-matrix majorant bounds the coefficient measures; compact-uniform smooth approximation of the continuous multiplier then proves convergence. The smooth product rule gives D(hα_m∧S)=α_m∧D(hS)=0, so D(hS_f)=0.

Choose cutting functions in the closed curve's ideal while avoiding every current component prime. A component of dimension greater than one cannot lie in the curve, so that ideal is not contained in any such prime. Finite avoidance over the infinite field supplies each function. After n−1 proper cuts, the resulting finite effective curve cycle contains every reduced component of the prescribed closed curve. Distinct resulting curve components intersect only in a finite rigid set. On an ordinary open excluding the other components, compact test lifting through its closed immersion separates its intrinsic equation with its actual positive weight. Rigid puncture removal, reconstructed in the main file, extends this equation over the intersections. Finally recombine the prescribed curve's own generic lengths. Thus D[h|C]=0 intrinsically for every closed pure analytic curve C, including curves contained in the ambient singular locus and nonreduced structures. No arbitrary quotient is declared S1 and no global multiplicity is divided out.

For the probe map, choose connected normal strict affinoid source and strict affinoid target neighbourhoods. Their bounded algebra map has two branches. If all pulled-back Tate coordinates are algebraic over K, they generate a finite field E inside the reduced source algebra. That field is complete and closed in the source Banach algebra; limits of polynomial partial sums show the entire bounded Tate map factors through E. The map is therefore rigid constant locally, including inseparable E/K.

Otherwise a pulled-back coordinate b is transcendental over K. At any rigid source point a, its value is algebraic over K. Its minimal polynomial P_a makes P_a(b) a nonzero nonunit in a one-dimensional domain. The quotient by it is a zero-dimensional strict affinoid and finite over K. The actual fibre over f(a), with its completed residue field, is a closed subspace of the corresponding scalar-extended finite zero algebra, hence has dimension zero. CLD11.4.5's Zariski upper semicontinuity and the strict Nullstellensatz then show that the positive-relative-dimension locus is empty: a nonempty closed locus would have a rigid point. The separated-target boundary equality makes the original map relatively boundaryless, so the finite-at-a-point criterion supplies actual analytic neighbourhoods on which it is finite. It does not require compactness of the original entire fibre.

Shrink the target to a strict affinoid neighbourhood and take the connected source component containing the chosen point. Its algebra B is normal and a domain. For A the target algebra, the prime kernel gives A_0=A/ker(A→B), a reduced strict affinoid domain algebra; B is finite integral over A_0 and both have dimension one. The closed analytic image C=M(A_0) is therefore a pure curve. Analytic surjectivity is checked at every image point c: lying-over supplies a nonzero finite fibre algebra over κ(ker c), extending to H(c) keeps it nonzero, and a finite residue field with its extending norm gives an actual analytic fibre point. The finite integral closure of A_0 embeds boundedly into B by normality, giving the finite normalization lift. No separability or finite-flatness assertion is used.

Pass now to the actual ordinary target interior V^o containing f(y). C^o=C∩V^o is closed in a good separated strict boundaryless pure ambient open and itself a good separated strict boundaryless pure curve. The reconstructed restriction lemma gives D[h|C^o]=0. Apply n1 directly over this same possibly imperfect field to recognize h|C^o. GR3.14(7) pulls back this already harmonic function to the ordinary source neighbourhood. The normalization of C^o is not asserted smooth over K and is unnecessary for this recognition step. Locality covers every analytic source point. GR3.4.2 and 3.12 identify the conclusion with Thuillier harmonicity on the smooth strict source; GR4.1.2 and 3.15 supply its classical and real-PL/GJR conclusions.

The complete proof, source statements and primary bodies are in P06.2-argument.md, with standalone P06.2-partial.tex and twice-compiled P06.2-partial.pdf. It supplies no current equation on X_L for arbitrary transcendental L/K and therefore does not establish classical pluriharmonicity of the original higher-dimensional h with all extension probes. It adds no result for non-strict ground-field source curves, ordinary smooth harmonic approximants, or two-sign ordinary positive-current regularization. task.problem:
Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct

vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for
every zero-current function. The gauges are not asserted to be logarithms of analytic units,
so this criterion does not manufacture global annular coordinates. Even when the full class
does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar
contraction with the radiance class vanishes. Its exact sequence also shows that an injective
contraction, and in particular the absence of parallel dual sections, forces unique descent of
every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen
aﬃne gauge splits this sequence.

                                               56

     For the three regularity conclusions, part of that monodromy obstruction can be removed.
In Book Corollary M.1.33, one analytic open cover of the original curve is allowed to coordinate
every annular stage after base change. On each member of the cover, the whole restricted
tower is an instance of the interleaved theorem; the local conclusions therefore glue even
though the annular coordinates, radii, and product trivializations need not agree on overlaps.
Thus curve-controlled locally twisted annular stages may occur at arbitrary levels. The result
deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations
available only over arbitrary opens of intermediate tower levels, because such opens need not
retain the preceding tower or its paracompactness hypotheses.
     There is also a nonproduct endpoint-base range. If the base is a positive- dimensional
standard strict endpoint polycylinder and the ﬁbre is a locally trivial standard strict open
polydisc, then Book Proposition M.1.37 pulls every full zero-current function back from the
explicit aﬃne combination of the base annular logarithms. Thus it is classically pluriharmonic,
locally R-PL, and GJR harmonic. This allows open, closed, and half-closed annuli in the base,
but still does not treat an annular ﬁbre, a ﬁbration without the displayed local product charts,
or an equation only on a strict radial core. The same formula persists through every ﬁnite
tower of the displayed locally trivial strict open-polydisc bundles: Book Corollary M.1.56
ﬁrst descends the function to the endpoint-polycylinder base and then applies the endpoint
classiﬁcation. Each level must carry the stated local product charts; the nontrivial tower
result retains the formula together with local R-PL and GJR harmonicity, by propagating its
local curve-product charts. This still does not cover annular ﬁbres or ﬁbrations without them.
     There is a further invariant nonproduct range. Let the base be a good, topologically sepa-
rated, strict, pure positive-dimensional open inverse image in the extended tropicalization of
a split toric variety, and let a locally trivial standard strict open-polydisc bundle carry a lift
of its maximal compact torus action. If the continuous zero-current function is invariant for
that lifted action, then Book Corollary M.1.63 ﬁrst descends it to an invariant zero-current
function on the toric base and then applies the split-toric boundary theorem. It is therefore
locally real-PL, Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ harmonic, and classically pluriharmonic. The action,
invariance, and actual local open-polydisc trivializations are hypotheses: this supplies no con-
clusion for noninvariant functions, nonsplit forms, annular ﬁbres, or arbitrary disc ﬁbrations.
The same conclusion persists through every ﬁnite tower of such bundles when the maximal
compact torus acts on every level and all bundle maps are equivariant: successive exact
descents preserve invariance and reduce to the same split-toric base theorem; see Book Corol-
lary M.1.64. The same bundle scope descends through a chosen complete extension that is the
completion of an algebraic extension when the base becomes the displayed split toric domain
and all three of the lifted action, invariance, and zero-current conditions hold upstairs; see
Book Corollary M.1.68. The corresponding ﬁnite-tower statement is Book Corollary M.1.69;
it requires the full compatible tower, action, invariance, and current equation after that chosen
extension. It does not manufacture the extension or bundle chart, and supplies no automatic
ascent of a downstairs current equality. Its analytic-local form Book Corollary M.1.70 requires
that displayed structure only near each point of the total space; it makes no assertion when
such neighbourhood data are absent. The same localisation is valid for ﬁnite towers: Book
Corollary M.1.71 requires a complete displayed tower near each point of the total space, with
the scalar-stable extension, the compatible action on every level, and equivariance of every
map. It supplies the same three conclusions locally, but does not create that tower or transfer
a downstairs current equation upstairs.
     The former third atom in this environment is now resolved. Book Theorem 19.3.4 proves
that every continuous current-psh function on every smooth proper algebraic curve over an
algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued ﬁeld is, locally on a strict aﬃnoid neigh-
bourhood, a uniformly convergent decreasing sequence of ordinary CLD-smooth psh func-
tions. Equivalently, current positivity, Thuillier subharmonicity, and the ﬁrst ordinary-smooth

decreasing-limit stage coincide in this scope. The proof passes through ﬁnite local tree skeleta,
rational strictiﬁcation of graph Laplacians, Riemann–Roch movement of residual divisors into
fresh disc directions, and smooth convex caps. The exact frozen statement and proof passed
production Rethlas run 20260827T090645Z_767cbf81c723, using gpt-5.6-sol at xhigh,
with ﬁnal verdict correct, zero critical errors, and zero gaps. The direct endpoint did not
assign an item identiﬁer.
    The formerly written harmonic-approximant strengthening is false: Book Proposi-
tion 19.3.2 constructs an integral PL weakly smooth harmonic function on a smooth proper
curve which is not even a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD-smooth harmonic functions.
Its ﬁxed-support argument uses zero curvature of every approximant and says nothing against
the now-proved psh regularization theorem, whose approximants carry positive curvature
in fresh directions. The exact-live proposition and proof passed production Rethlas run

notes.text:
The mathematical claim is the following curve-scope theorem. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued field, X any good separated strict boundaryless K-analytic space pure of dimension one, U any ordinary open in X, and h:U→R continuous and finite. If the actual ordinary CLD current D[h]=d'd''[h] vanishes, then h is GR-harmonic and classically pluriharmonic, G-locally real PL, and GJR harmonic. No perfectness, reducedness, normality, global properness, algebraicity, or input scalar-stability hypothesis is imposed. Classical pluriharmonicity has the full quantifiers: after every complete analytic extension L/K and every analytic curve map Y→U_L, both pulled-back signs are GR-subharmonic.

The authoritative complete draft is P06.2-argument.md in the assigned workspace. Its standalone typesetting is P06.2-partial.tex and its twice-compiled PDF is P06.2-partial.pdf. status.json has exactly id, status, exact_result, proof_file, concrete_gaps and records status=partial. self-audit.md, research-notes.md, source-manifest.json, and evidence/ contain the dependency audit, failed routes, hashes, environment, commands, and outputs. Rerun from the workspace with python3 prepare.py followed by python3 build-and-check.py. The workspace is /workspace/research/campaigns/round-13/P06.2-arbitrary-field-curve-recognition-continuation/artifacts/codex-mNUPp2.

The first proof obligation is ordinary-current transport. On a pure curve, vanishing means ∫hDψ=0 for every compact ordinary smooth scalar test ψ; the unknown Hessian is not presumed to be a measure. For a finite Galois scalar extension, average a test over the finite group using real coefficients. Full-fibre shrinking gives unit-moment descriptions near every downstairs point. Approximate their Euclidean coefficients through order two by polynomials. Scalar polarization expresses every averaged mixed polynomial as a finite combination of traces of powers of logarithms of product units. The orbit polynomial has downstairs coefficients. Its Newton hull expresses these traces as piecewise polynomial functions of the nonzero coefficient valuations; coefficients vanishing at the selected point are omitted only after a strict inequality proves they cannot enter the lower hull.

Those Newton-hull functions are C1: when collinear segments merge, their gradients telescope. Their locally bounded chamber Hessians have no singular face contribution. Mollification converges in the tangent Hessian on every calibrated curve segment, including segments wholly contained in collision walls. On an enlarged moment chart, the positive top form Σd't_i∧d''t_i dominates the differentiated error on the actual supporting skeleton. Bounded convergence yields carrier total-variation convergence before any signed pushforward. Inner cutoffs may depend on polynomial degree, but every approximate support stays inside one fixed outer compact set. Thus pairing the error with any continuous finite h tends to zero. CLD14.3.6 and 15.3.1 transport pulled-back smooth top measures with no scalar degree factor. The separate same-carrier field-restriction calibration has the full finite degree; it is used only to justify the group action on the upstairs pairing. This proves finite separable ascent, with normal-closure descent handling non-Galois stages.

For a finite purely inseparable extension F/K, choose q=p^e with F^q⊂K. In the actual algebra A⊗K F every element has its qth power in A. Scalar projection is a homeomorphism, and each upstairs unit logarithm is q^-1 times a downstairs unit logarithm. Consequently compact scalar tests descend exactly. Every finite algebraic extension is treated through its actual embedded separable/purely inseparable tower, including all nilpotents.

For L equal to the completion of an algebraic extension M/K, completed-tensor density approximates finitely many analytic functions by functions over a finite embedded stage. A positive lower bound for the weighted maximum of a rational system's denominator and numerators makes sufficiently small perturbations preserve both the full weak conjunction and its strict locus exactly. On a compact rational domain, approximation below each unit's positive minimum preserves its norm exactly. The same smooth coefficient therefore defines a finite-stage scalar section whose pullback is the original section. A common finite stage and an explicit finite compact partition produce exact global descent of every compact ordinary scalar test. Compact inverse images and local purity are checked separately. The calibrated smooth top-measure identity then proves completed-algebraic ascent and descent of the actual current equation.

The second obligation is recognition, separate from transport. Equip an algebraic closure of K with its extending valuation and complete it to C. The draft proves C algebraically closed: approximate any monic polynomial by monic polynomials over the algebraic closure with rapidly decreasing coefficient errors; recursively choose roots whose successive distances tend to zero using the factored evaluation bound. Their bounded Cauchy sequence converges to a root. C is complete and nontrivially valued because it contains K isometrically. The transport theorem therefore gives D[h_C]=0 on the actual pure curve U_C.

For algebraically closed recognition, CLD16.6.3 decomposes integration into reduced components with their original generic Artinian lengths. Closed-embedding compact tests lift by analytic-unit lifting and compact cutoffs. Away from the finite rigid intersections, the current equation separates each component with its actual positive weight. Rigid scalar test germs are locally constant: the minimal polynomial of a unit's value forces its norm to remain constant on a sufficiently small neighbourhood. At a rigid point a, a regular analytic function with singleton zero fibre gives shrinking smooth cutoffs χ_m with uniformly bounded variation of Dχ_m and zero integral. CLD14.7.2 applies with target dimension one and an already S1 source; the bound contains the actual length times the full residue-field degree. A current supported at a is therefore cψ(a) on scalar tests, and continuity gives |c|≤M sup_supportχ_m|h-h(a)|→0. This removes rigid punctures without assuming D[h] is a measure.

Normalization is an actual isomorphism outside a locally finite rigid set: a common regular denominator clears its finite integral-closure generators. Transport on that isomorphism locus followed by puncture removal proves the upstairs equation. Over the algebraically closed field the normalization is smooth. Van der Put's Theorem1.1 applies only to a connected normal one-dimensional strict affinoid over that algebraically closed complete field. Thuillier's explicit Berkovich-domain formulation and the separated boundaryless interior equality identify actual ordinary neighbourhoods with ordinary opens of smooth proper algebraic curves. Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, Theorem4.7 applies exactly there: a continuous current-psh function is Thuillier-subharmonic. Her algebraic moment tests are ordinary analytic CLD tests with the same canonical integration. The zero equation supplies positivity for both signs. Dirichlet comparison recognizes harmonicity. GR3.14(7) descends already recognized harmonicity through normalization and the reduction immersion.

Full field quantifiers are checked after recognition. For any analytic extension L/K, embed the algebraic closure of K into an algebraic closure of L and complete the latter to a common complete field F containing C and L isometrically. F/C is not asserted algebraic. GR3.5(7), whose full proof is included, descends subharmonicity using this joint field and compact harmonic-majorant comparison on smooth strict probes. GR3.14(6), 4.1.2, 4.2(5), and 7.2(6) then give the full recognized-function descent. GR3.15 applies over the original nontrivially valued K to every strict analytic curve and yields real PL plus numerical triviality of all residual classes, precisely GJR harmonicity. notes.detailedSummary: Using n1's arbitrary-field intrinsic recognition, the draft proves harmonicity of h∘f for every analytic K-map from a separated smooth strict curve into an ordinary open of a pure ambient space in the original P06.2 scope. It reconstructs intrinsic restriction to closed analytic curves through positive effective cuts with actual component lengths, continuous multiplication of positive weak limits, an S1 Poincare–Lelong proof, compact test lifting, and rigid puncture removal. The local-image proof gives either a rigid constant map or an actual finite map onto a reduced closed pure curve image, with analytic surjectivity and a finite normalization lift checked. Applying recognition directly to the image avoids assuming its normalization smooth over imperfect K. The resulting probe function is Thuillier/GR harmonic, classically pluriharmonic, G-locally real PL, and GJR harmonic. Probes into scalar-extended higher-dimensional spaces remain outside this conclusion.
notes.text:
Assuming the curve theorem proved in n1, the additional mathematical claim is this: over every complete nontrivially valued K, let X be good separated strict boundaryless and pure of dimension n≥1, U⊂X ordinary open, and h:U→R continuous finite with actual ordinary CLD D[h]=0. For every analytic K-map f:Y→U from a separated smooth strict K-analytic curve, h∘f is Thuillier harmonic and GR-harmonic, classically pluriharmonic on Y, G-locally real PL, and GJR harmonic. Smooth includes absence of absolute analytic boundary. This is Theorem P in P06.2-argument.md; it uses n1's result and no previous solver-note theorem.

The restriction argument is intrinsic. On the ordinary interior of a strict affinoid neighbourhood, decompose the ambient integration cycle into reduced pure components with their actual generic lengths. Reduced noetherian rings satisfy S1 by finite prime avoidance. The draft proves Poincare–Lelong on such S1 sources from CLD14.7.2 with target dimension one and Green's formula. Its compact calibrated product near f=0 retains the actual zero-fibre lengths; the inner face gives the divisor integral and side faces vanish by dimension. The unsupported assertion in CLD16.7.5 that one regular element forces an arbitrary ring to be S1 is excluded.

For a regular cutting function on every component of a positive r-dimensional integration cycle S, use smooth convex truncations w_m of log|f| and the positive doubly closed form α_m=Dw_m. The currents α_m∧S converge to the effective component divisor cycle S_f. Continuous multiplication preserves this positive weak convergence: for a fixed compact symmetric test, a positive smooth coefficient-matrix majorant bounds the coefficient measures; compact-uniform smooth approximation of the continuous multiplier then proves convergence. The smooth product rule gives D(hα_m∧S)=α_m∧D(hS)=0, so D(hS_f)=0.

Choose cutting functions in the closed curve's ideal while avoiding every current component prime. A component of dimension greater than one cannot lie in the curve, so that ideal is not contained in any such prime. Finite avoidance over the infinite field supplies each function. After n−1 proper cuts, the resulting finite effective curve cycle contains every reduced component of the prescribed closed curve. Distinct resulting curve components intersect only in a finite rigid set. On an ordinary open excluding the other components, compact test lifting through its closed immersion separates its intrinsic equation with its actual positive weight. Rigid puncture removal, reconstructed in the main file, extends this equation over the intersections. Finally recombine the prescribed curve's own generic lengths. Thus D[h|C]=0 intrinsically for every closed pure analytic curve C, including curves contained in the ambient singular locus and nonreduced structures. No arbitrary quotient is declared S1 and no global multiplicity is divided out.

For the probe map, choose connected normal strict affinoid source and strict affinoid target neighbourhoods. Their bounded algebra map has two branches. If all pulled-back Tate coordinates are algebraic over K, they generate a finite field E inside the reduced source algebra. That field is complete and closed in the source Banach algebra; limits of polynomial partial sums show the entire bounded Tate map factors through E. The map is therefore rigid constant locally, including inseparable E/K.

Otherwise a pulled-back coordinate b is transcendental over K. At any rigid source point a, its value is algebraic over K. Its minimal polynomial P_a makes P_a(b) a nonzero nonunit in a one-dimensional domain. The quotient by it is a zero-dimensional strict affinoid and finite over K. The actual fibre over f(a), with its completed residue field, is a closed subspace of the corresponding scalar-extended finite zero algebra, hence has dimension zero. CLD11.4.5's Zariski upper semicontinuity and the strict Nullstellensatz then show that the positive-relative-dimension locus is empty: a nonempty closed locus would have a rigid point. The separated-target boundary equality makes the original map relatively boundaryless, so the finite-at-a-point criterion supplies actual analytic neighbourhoods on which it is finite. It does not require compactness of the original entire fibre.

Shrink the target to a strict affinoid neighbourhood and take the connected source component containing the chosen point. Its algebra B is normal and a domain. For A the target algebra, the prime kernel gives A_0=A/ker(A→B), a reduced strict affinoid domain algebra; B is finite integral over A_0 and both have dimension one. The closed analytic image C=M(A_0) is therefore a pure curve. Analytic surjectivity is checked at every image point c: lying-over supplies a nonzero finite fibre algebra over κ(ker c), extending to H(c) keeps it nonzero, and a finite residue field with its extending norm gives an actual analytic fibre point. The finite integral closure of A_0 embeds boundedly into B by normality, giving the finite normalization lift. No separability or finite-flatness assertion is used.

Pass now to the actual ordinary target interior V^o containing f(y). C^o=C∩V^o is closed in a good separated strict boundaryless pure ambient open and itself a good separated strict boundaryless pure curve. The reconstructed restriction lemma gives D[h|C^o]=0. Apply n1 directly over this same possibly imperfect field to recognize h|C^o. GR3.14(7) pulls back this already harmonic function to the ordinary source neighbourhood. The normalization of C^o is not asserted smooth over K and is unnecessary for this recognition step. Locality covers every analytic source point. GR3.4.2 and 3.12 identify the conclusion with Thuillier harmonicity on the smooth strict source; GR4.1.2 and 3.15 supply its classical and real-PL/GJR conclusions.

The complete proof, source statements and primary bodies are in P06.2-argument.md, with standalone P06.2-partial.tex and twice-compiled P06.2-partial.pdf. Rerun python3 prepare.py and python3 build-and-check.py in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-13/P06.2-arbitrary-field-curve-recognition-continuation/artifacts/codex-mNUPp2. The shared build evidence reports 128 pages and clean final TeX diagnostics; those checks do not verify the theorem.

This result is strictly ground-field recognition of probe functions. It supplies no current equation on X_L for arbitrary transcendental L/K and therefore does not establish classical pluriharmonicity of the original higher-dimensional h with all extension probes. It adds no result for non-strict ground-field source curves, ordinary smooth harmonic approximants, or two-sign ordinary positive-current regularization. Original arbitrary-dimensional P06.2 remains open and candidate remains false.

These are useful routes to a finite factorization onto a closed curve image, but their conditions must be established on the actual source and target neighbourhoods; compactness is not automatic for an arbitrary curve map. The present proof does not supply that factorization for every probe. Where such a factorization is supplied, finite affinoid algebra maps do give a closed analytic image by their kernel. One still needs curve harmonic recognition and harmonic pullback in the relevant field and boundary scope. Theorem C is about normalization and does not handle arbitrary finite covers or arbitrary curve morphisms. No example with higher-dimensional analytic-Zariski-dense local image is asserted here.
1088:Classical psh is defined by **every analytic complete-field extension and every curve map**: Gubler--Rabinoff, arXiv:2506.13548v2, Definition 4.1 and Definition 3.4. Both signs must pass these tests for classical pluriharmonicity (Definition 7.1). The precise definitions are checked in `sources/GR-2506.13548.txt`. Our equation on $X$ supplies none on a newly base-changed $X_L$. Theorem A can be applied upstairs only once the upstairs equation has been separately proved. A finite ground-field restriction on the same carrier, or a top-form measure pushforward computation, would not supply that ascent. No graph/product-current ascent is used.
1090:The published smooth-proper-curve comparison described in the catalogue is not imported here as a theorem on all analytic curves or all residue fields. We have proved an intrinsic equation on the closed curve and its normalization; recognition of every such equation as harmonic, with the required extension quantifiers, is a separate obligation. The GJR real-PL and weakly smooth results likewise cannot be invoked before their regularity hypotheses hold. Ordinary smooth, weakly smooth, and G-local real-PL conclusions remain distinct; none is asserted for the general $h$ in Theorem A.
1092:Finally, no two-sign positive-current regularization has been constructed. The smooth convex functions in Lemma 4 are truncations of a **unit logarithm** that construct a divisor cycle; they are not approximants to $h$ or $-h$. Fixed-test scalar approximation in Lemma 1 only controls an error and is not a positivity-to-psh recognition theorem. Thus the scalar-current ascent gate and the two-sign regularization gate remain separately unresolved.
